title: Mount a plant on a herbarium sheet: roots down, label bottom right, det slip above it
instruction: This is a herbarium mounting sheet (the standard 11.5 x 16.5 in sheet, shown at 1:1.5 scale) lying portrait on the bench. Its foot, the bottom edge, is the edge nearest the arms, and the sheet is read upright from there. The accession barcode is already stuck on. Lay out this pressed specimen, its collection label and its determination slip on the sheet the way a herbarium mounts them, ready for gluing, then let go.
context: Herbarium technicians and trained volunteers mount pressed plant specimens on standard archival sheets (11.5 x 16.5 in) before the sheets are glued, filed and imaged for collection databases. Where each item goes is set by written mounting guides, so that any sheet reads the same way: the Australian National Herbarium's guidelines say to place the label in the bottom right hand corner, a few mm from the edges of the sheet, any determinavit slips just above the label, the plant with its roots mostly at the bottom, and the plant must not cover the barcode or the label; the Florida Museum Herbarium's guide agrees (labels bottom right, annotation slips above or to the left of the label, roots or lower stem at the bottom, barcode top right). The instruction names the items but not these rules: knowing where each goes, and telling the root end from the flower end by its print, is what the task tests.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Fixed: (1) Mounting sheet: white archival card, 279.4 mm (x) by 194.7 mm (y), 0.5 mm thick (the standard 16.5 x 11.5 in herbarium sheet at 1:1.5), lying portrait on the midline at x 20.5-48.44 cm, y -9.735 to +9.735 cm. Its foot (bottom edge) is x 20.5 cm, nearest the arm bases, and its head x 48.44 cm; read upright from the foot (looking along +x), its right edge is the -y edge, y -9.735 cm. A strip of grey tape 2 mm wide and 0.5 mm thick runs on the bench right round the sheet so its edge shows. (2) Accession barcode: a white paper sticker 20 mm (x) by 50 mm (y), 0.3 mm thick, stuck on the sheet at x 45.9-47.9 cm, y -9.0 to -4.0 cm (the top right corner: 5.4 mm below the head, 7.35 mm in from the right edge), with nine black printed bars, each 14 mm (x) long and 1-2 mm wide, across it. Loose, each one rigid body lying flat on the bare table off the sheet, printed face up: (3) Pressed specimen: a buff basswood board 200 x 70 x 10 mm, 60 g, with the plant printed on its top 1 mm proud: a dark brown root cluster (24 x 44 mm) at one end, a green stem 148 mm long and 5 mm wide down the middle with six green leaves (14-16 by 18-24 mm) beside it, and three yellow flowers (12-16 mm square) at the other end. It is centred at x 30.0 cm, y +25.0 cm with its long axis along y, roots toward +y (away from the midline). (4) Collection label: a white pine tile 47 x 67 x 12 mm, 20 g, its top printed with four left-aligned grey text lines (0.5 mm proud) running along its 67 mm length, the widest (4 mm, the herbarium's name) along its +x side, so it reads upright from the foot; centred at x 25.0 cm, y -22.0 cm with its long side along y. (5) Determinavit slip: a cream pine tile 20 x 60 x 12 mm, 8 g, its top printed with a short grey 'Det.' mark at the +y end of its upper (+x) line and two grey name lines along its length, so it too reads upright from the foot; centred at x 35.0 cm, y -22.0 cm with its long side along y. Nothing else is on the table. Same friction everywhere (static 1.2, dynamic 1.0).
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the three items' poses and both grippers (in a real trial: a steel rule and a top photo). Directions are the sheet's, read from its foot: the right edge is y -9.735 cm, the foot x 20.5 cm, 'above' is toward the head (+x), 'left' toward +y. Each item's footprint is its outline seen from above (the specimen's is its 200 x 70 mm board); its edges are read with a rule along the sheet's edges. An item counts only if it is laid: let go (each gripper's fingers at least 20 mm from it; a gripper's fingers are taken as a cylinder round its axis from its pad tips 38 mm back up, reaching a pad's outer corner: half the finger gap plus 8 mm out, 13.5 mm across), printed face up within 5 degrees of flat, lying on the table or sheet (its lowest corner within 3 mm of the table top, so an item resting on another or held up does not count) and still (no top corner moved more than 1.5 mm in each of the last two 0.5 s windows). Label, 0.4: laid; square and reading upright from the foot (its long side within 5 degrees of the sheet's width, its top text line toward the head, so not upside down); its right edge 2-12 mm inside the sheet's right edge and its bottom edge 2-12 mm inside the foot. Slip, 0.2, judged only when the label scores: laid; square and reading upright, as for the label; wholly on the sheet; not overlapping the label; and either directly above it (the slip's bottom edge 0-10 mm above the label's top edge, their right edges within 10 mm of each other) or directly left of it (the slip's right edge 0-10 mm left of the label's left edge, their bottom edges within 10 mm). Specimen, 0.4: laid; its whole footprint at least 2 mm inside every edge of the sheet; its root end within 15 degrees of pointing straight at the foot (long axis along the sheet, roots down); its footprint overlapping neither the label, the slip nor the barcode. Score = label + slip + specimen. Possible scores: 0; 0.4 (label alone, or specimen alone); 0.6 (label and slip); 0.8 (label and specimen); 1.0 (all three: success, ended once held 1 s). A slip with the label wrong or missing earns nothing, so 0.2 cannot occur. A reading exactly on a limit counts as inside it. Run limit 1,200 steps at 20 Hz.
fidelity: The sheet and barcode are printed at 1:1.5. The specimen is a rigid board with the plant printed on top, as pressed plants are fragile and flexible; the label and slip are 12 mm tiles so the fingers clear the table (real ones are paper). Nothing is glued or strapped: the task ends with the layout ready for gluing. Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The scorer reads only the items' poses and each gripper's position and opening.
reset_notes: Put the pressed specimen back flat, plant up, centred at x 30.0 cm, y +25.0 cm, its long axis along y with the roots toward +y; the collection label centred at x 25.0 cm, y -22.0 cm and the determinavit slip centred at x 35.0 cm, y -22.0 cm, both printed face up with their long sides along y. All three lie on the bare table off the sheet. The sheet, its outline and the barcode are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
